t: Jewish tradition ascribes the Torah to Moses, while most scholars see the books as composed and edited in stages over several hundred years, receiving their final shape in the Second Temple period.
Its three parts, the Torah, the Nevi'im and the Ketuvim, reached canonical status one after another, and scholars disagree on when the canon was fixed.
The Masoretic Text of the 7th to 10th centuries CE is the form authoritative in Judaism today, and it differs in places from older witnesses such as the Septuagint and the Dead Sea Scrolls.
dyk: The Hebrew Bible has 8,679 distinct words, of which 1,480 occur only once. The count of 24 books is somewhat arbitrary, since the twelve Minor Prophets are counted as a single book.
ev: Scholars estimate that the Jacob tradition of Genesis 25–35 was first written down in the north, probably at the sanctuary of Bethel
The northern Kingdom of Samaria is conquered by the Neo-Assyrian Empire
The Kingdom of Judah is conquered by the Neo-Babylonian Empire, the Temple is destroyed and many Judaeans are exiled to Babylon
Cyrus the Great of Persia conquers Babylon and grants the Judaean exiles freedom to return to Zion
The Book of Daniel is written, and is not grouped with the Prophets, presumably because that collection was already fixed
Some scholars place the completion of the canon here, while others date it earlier; rabbis between 70 and 100 CE had debated which books make the hands unclean
The compilation of the Masoretic Text by Jewish scribes and scholars begins, a work of the 7th to 10th centuries CE that added vowel markings to the text
The Jewish Publication Society publishes its Tanakh, replacing its translation of 1917

f.made: The Israelites, in Samaria and Judah and later in exile and the Second Temple period; tradition ascribes the Torah to Moses, at least 73 psalms to David and three books to Solomon, while scholars see composition and editing in stages
f.form: Twenty-four books in three divisions (Torah, Nevi'im, Ketuvim), mostly in Biblical Hebrew with a few passages in Biblical Aramaic; prose, poetry, law, prophecy and wisdom writing
f.where: Read in Jewish and Christian worship and study worldwide; the Aleppo Codex and the Leningrad Codex are Tiberian Masoretic manuscripts; other witnesses include the Septuagint, the Samaritan Pentateuch and the Dead Sea Scrolls
f.known: The Torah and the Law of Moses; the covenant between God and Israel; monotheism; the Psalms; wisdom books such as Proverbs and Ecclesiastes; the prophets; the Masoretic Text; the Septuagint translation
